entry.title: Day 10 — Legacy Systems (The Old Bridge)
entry.summary:
The forest grows darker as Gord and Rothütle push deeper, the trees closing in like ancient sentinels. Rothütle checks every trunk and shadow nervously. "So, how did my shadow turn against me?" he asks, voice low. "It was a manifestation of the prisoner I talked about," Gord explains. "The old magic is failing." "You should perhaps try to use some new magic then," Rothütle suggests. "Crossing this bridge is risky," Gord warns. Rothütle hesitates. "I'm not sure if I want to cross it or meet another one of your friends." Gord inspects the bridge carefully. "We have no choice. We need to get to the other side." As they step onto the bridge, it creaks ominously under their weight. Halfway across, a plank snaps, and Rothütle stumbles, grabbing the ropes for support. Tip of the day: Legacy systems can fail catastrophically under load. Keep your infrastructure updated and modernized to avoid sudden breakdowns. Old, unmaintained components behave like the collapsing bridge:
they don't break slowly — they break suddenly, and only when you depend on them most. There is an old saying in software engineering: "If it works, don't touch it." That's a dangerous mindset in security, as legacy systems often harbor unpatched vulnerabilities and can contain well-known CVEs. Those systems should be maintained at least in the following ways: Regularly audit legacy systems for vulnerabilities and performance issues. Plan and execute modernization strategies to replace or upgrade outdated components. Rebuild the Docker images and update dependencies frequently, when possible. If the system is not maintainable, try to replace it with modern, supported alternatives. My book Docker and Kubernetes Security is currently 40% off.

entry.title: Why I Chose GoatCounter for my GitHub Pages Site
entry.summary:
Simple Analytics for GitHub Pages: Why I Chose GoatCounter
Adding analytics to a static site usually ends in one of two ways: Google Analytics: A privacy nightmare that requires a GDPR cookie banner. No Analytics: You fly blind and never know if anyone visited. I needed a middle ground for my GitHub Pages site. I looked at the big three options. GA4 is overkill. It tracks everything, sells the data, and forces you to annoy users with cookie consent popups. I just want to know how many people clicked my "Install" button. Cloudflare offers great free analytics. The Problem: It expects you to own the domain. github.io subdomain, I cannot easily proxy my DNS through Cloudflare. Without DNS control, the setup becomes friction. I wanted "drop-in" simplicity. Umami is fantastic and open-source. The Problem: Hosting. GoatCounter hit the sweet spot. Hosted: No server to manage. Free: Generous tier for non-commercial projects. Privacy: No cookies. No GDPR banners required. Universal: Works on any domain, including github.io. The setup took 2 minutes. Sign up at GoatCounter and get your link context. We added a single JS file to our docs/ folder to keep it clean. docs/index.html: <script data-goatcounter="https://your-code.goatcounter.com/count" async src="count.js"></script>
We host the count.js locally to avoid external dependencies blocking the main thread, though you can load it from their CDN too. Check out the Git-Scope Docs to see it in action.

Roman numerals are represented by seven different symbols: I, V, X, L, C, D and M. I = 1 For example, 2 is written as II in Roman numeral, just two ones added together. 12 is written as XII, which is simply X + II. The number 27 is written as XXVII, which is XX + V + II. Roman numerals are usually written largest to smallest from left to right. However, the numeral for four is not IIII. Instead, the number four is written as IV. entry.title: Como Economizar no Delivery de Comida: Dicas Práticas para o Dia a Dia
entry.summary: O delivery de comida se tornou parte essencial da rotina dos brasileiros. Com a correria do dia a dia, pedir comida por aplicativo oferece praticidade e variedade sem precisar sair de casa. Mas como aproveitar esse serviço sem pesar no bolso? Uma das melhores formas de economizar é ficar atento às promoções dos aplicativos. Muitas plataformas oferecem cupons de desconto, cashback e frete grátis em determinados horários ou dias da semana. Algumas também têm programas de fidelidade que valem a pena para quem pede com frequência. A Keeta Entrega Grátis é um exemplo de como as plataformas estão trabalhando para tornar o delivery mais acessível aos consumidores brasileiros, oferecendo opções que cabem no orçamento. Fazer pedidos em grupo com amigos, familiares ou colegas de trabalho pode reduzir significativamente o custo do frete por pessoa. Além disso, muitos restaurantes oferecem descontos em pedidos acima de determinado valor, tornando o pedido coletivo ainda mais vantajoso. Antes de finalizar seu pedido, vale a pena comparar preços entre diferentes restaurantes e plataformas. O mesmo prato pode ter valores diferentes dependendo do estabelecimento. Também fique atento ao tempo de entrega e às avaliações de outros usuários. Os horários de pico geralmente têm taxas de entrega mais altas devido à alta demanda. Se possível, peça fora desses períodos. Além de economizar, você pode receber seu pedido mais rapidamente. Muitos restaurantes oferecem combos promocionais que saem mais em conta do que pedir os itens separadamente. Pratos executivos durante a semana também costumam ter preços mais acessíveis. Pedir comida por delivery não precisa ser um luxo. Com planejamento e atenção às promoções, é possível aproveitar a comodidade desse serviço de forma econômica. O segredo está em ser estratégico e aproveitar as oportunidades que surgem nos aplicativos.

entry.title: Booking.com built agentic AI before 'agents' existed: Here's how it scaled with small models for speed, big models for trust
entry.summary:
When many enterprises weren’t even thinking about agentic behaviors or infrastructures, Booking.com had already “stumbled” into them with its homegrown conversational recommendation system.
This early experimentation has allowed the company to take a step back and avoid getting swept up in the frantic AI agent hype. Instead, it is taking a disciplined, layered, modular approach to model development: small, travel-specific models for cheap, fast inference; larger large language models (LLMs) for reasoning and understanding; and domain-tuned evaluations built in-house when precision is critical.
